## Purpose

Download simple state outlines for **Texas** and **Michigan** with the
[`tigris`](https://github.com/walkerke/tigris) package and export each one as an
SVG file in this directory (`designs/coasters_blue_wave/`). The SVGs are sized
in millimetres so they import into Carbide Create at a known size.

Notes on the choices below:

- `cb = TRUE` uses the Census *cartographic boundary* file, which is clipped to
  the shoreline. The full TIGER/Line state polygons include Great Lakes water,
  which would make Michigan look like a big block.
- `resolution = "20m"` is the most generalized version, which suits a 3" coaster
  and a 1/32" end mill.
- Each state is projected to a local equal-area / conformal CRS so the shape
  isn't stretched the way raw latitude/longitude would be.
- Small islands (Isle Royale, Beaver Island, the Texas barrier islands, etc.) are
  dropped below a size threshold. Set `min_part_frac <- 0` to keep everything.

## Download and export

```{r}
#| label: state-outlines

library(tigris)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

out_dir <- "."          # Quarto runs chunks in the document's own directory

# Export settings ----------------------------------------------------------
width_mm      <- 45     # width of each exported outline in millimetres
min_part_frac <- 0.02   # drop polygon parts smaller than 2% of the largest part
simplify_m    <- 250    # extra simplification tolerance in metres (0 = none)

state_specs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,      ~abbr, ~crs,
  "texas",    "TX",  3083,   # NAD83 / Texas Centric Albers Equal Area
  "michigan", "MI",  3078    # NAD83 / Michigan Oblique Mercator
)

# Download -----------------------------------------------------------------
states_cb <- states(cb = TRUE, resolution = "20m", year = 2023)

# Helpers ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Keep the main land masses of a (multi)polygon; drop small islands
keep_main_parts <- function(geom, min_frac) {
  parts <- st_cast(st_geometry(geom), "POLYGON")
  areas <- as.numeric(st_area(parts))
  parts[areas >= min_frac * max(areas)] |> st_union()
}

# Write an sf polygon geometry (projected, metres) to an SVG sized in mm
write_state_svg <- function(geom, file, width_mm) {
  bb    <- st_bbox(geom)
  scale <- width_mm / as.numeric(bb["xmax"] - bb["xmin"])
  h_mm  <- as.numeric(bb["ymax"] - bb["ymin"]) * scale

  # one row per vertex; L1 = ring within polygon, L2 = polygon
  xy <- st_coordinates(st_cast(st_geometry(geom), "POLYGON"))
  xy <- as.data.frame(xy) |>
    mutate(x = (X - bb["xmin"]) * scale,
           y = (bb["ymax"] - Y) * scale)          # SVG y runs downward

  rings <- split(xy, list(xy$L2, xy$L1), drop = TRUE)
  d <- vapply(rings, function(r) {
    pts <- sprintf("%.3f,%.3f", r$x, r$y)
    paste0("M", pts[1], " L", paste(pts[-1], collapse = " "), " Z")
  }, character(1))

  svg <- c(
    '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no"?>',
    sprintf(paste0('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" version="1.1" ',
                   'width="%.3fmm" height="%.3fmm" viewBox="0 0 %.3f %.3f">'),
            width_mm, h_mm, width_mm, h_mm),
    sprintf('  <path d="%s" fill="black" fill-rule="evenodd" stroke="none"/>',
            paste(d, collapse = " ")),
    "</svg>"
  )
  writeLines(svg, file)
  invisible(c(width_mm = width_mm, height_mm = h_mm))
}

# Export -------------------------------------------------------------------
sizes <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(state_specs)), function(i) {
  s <- state_specs[i, ]
  geom <- states_cb |>
    filter(STUSPS == s$abbr) |>
    st_transform(s$crs) |>
    keep_main_parts(min_part_frac)
  if (simplify_m > 0) geom <- st_simplify(geom, preserveTopology = TRUE, dTolerance = simplify_m)

  file <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(s$name, "_outline.svg"))
  dims <- write_state_svg(geom, file, width_mm)
  tibble::tibble(state = s$name, file = file,
                 width_mm = dims[["width_mm"]], height_mm = round(dims[["height_mm"]], 1))
})
bind_rows(sizes)
```

## Preview

```{r}
#| label: preview
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
for (s in state_specs$name) {
  states_cb |>
    filter(STUSPS == state_specs$abbr[state_specs$name == s]) |>
    st_transform(state_specs$crs[state_specs$name == s]) |>
    keep_main_parts(min_part_frac) |>
    plot(col = "grey20", border = NA, main = tools::toTitleCase(s))
}
```
